notes: Full description: pkix-lint/tests/cabf_tls_br_tests.rs — the SHA-1 prohibited lint (Sha1ProhibitedLint) has no direct negative test using an actual SHA-1-signed certificate. The tests at lines 163-221 only test pass cases (SHA-256 certs) and an OID identity logic check. The sha1_prohibited_oid_detection_logic test at line 201 merely verifies that SHA-1 OIDs parse and differ from SHA-256 OIDs — it does not actually run the lint against a cert signed with SHA-1 and verify the Error result. The test file header comment at line 7-8 says 'Fixture certs are pre-generated DER files verified with openssl x509 -text.' No sha1-signed fixture exists, so no real negative test is possible without creating one. Fix: Generate a SHA-1 signed fixture cert (openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -sha1 -x509 ...) and add test sha1_prohibited_error_on_sha1_cert() verifying LintResult::Error is returned. Alternatively, construct synthetic DER that sets the signatureAlgorithm OID to sha1WithRSAEncryption. Priority: P3 (missing negative test; the lint's positive path is exercised but negative path is not).
title: FINDING: cabf_tls_br_tests missing negative test for SHA-1 signature cert
